RALEIGH, N.C.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Ralliant Corporation (“Ralliant” or the “Company”) (NYSE: RAL) announced today that its Board of Directors has approved a quarterly cash dividend of $0.05 per share on its common stock, payable on December 23, 2026, to stockholders of record as of the close of business on December 8, 2026.

About Ralliant

Ralliant is a global provider of precision technologies that specializes in designing, developing, manufacturing and servicing precision instruments and highly engineered products. Ralliant’s two strategic reporting segments — Sensors & Safety Systems and Test & Measurement — include well-known brands with leading positions in their markets. The Company’s businesses empower engineers with precision technologies essential for breakthrough innovation that brings advanced technologies to the market faster and more efficiently. With over 150 years of operating experience and enduring customer trust, we are known for delivering innovative, high-quality products with the precision that mission-critical systems demand. Ralliant is headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina, and employs a team of approximately 7,000 research and development, manufacturing, sales, distribution, service and administrative employees. The Company’s global footprint enables a unique 'engineer to engineer' approach, which allows it to build enduring trust, credibility, and partnerships with customers across both Fortune 1000 companies and next-generation start-up enterprises. With a culture rooted in continuous improvement, the core of the Company’s operating model is the Ralliant Business System. For more information please visit: www.ralliant.com.

NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Citibank, N.A. is announcing the redemption, in whole, constituting $2,000,000,000 of its 5.488% Notes due 2026 (the “fixed rate notes”) (ISIN: US17325FBC14) and $500,000,000 of its Floating Rate Notes due 2026 (the “floating rate notes” and together with the fixed rate notes, the “notes”) (ISIN: US17325FBD96).

The redemption date for the notes is November 4, 2026 (the “redemption date”). The cash redemption price for the notes payable on the redemption date will equal par plus accrued and unpaid interest to, but excluding, the redemption date.

The redemptions announced today are consistent with Citibank's liability management strategy and reflect its ongoing efforts to enhance the efficiency of its funding and capital structure. Citibank will continue to consider opportunities to redeem or repurchase securities, based on several factors, including without limitation, the economic value, regulatory changes, potential impact on Citibank's net interest margin and borrowing costs, the overall remaining tenor of Citibank's debt portfolio, capital impact, as well as overall market conditions.

Beginning on the redemption date, interest will no longer accrue on the notes.

Citibank, N.A. is the paying agent for the notes.

About Citi

Citi is a preeminent banking partner for institutions with cross-border needs, a global leader in wealth management and a valued personal bank in its home market of the United States. Citi does business in more than 180 countries and jurisdictions, providing corporations, governments, investors, institutions and individuals with a broad range of financial products and services.

The acquisition expands Arch’s capabilities in the automotive Finance and Insurance market

NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Arch Insurance North America (Arch Insurance, Arch), today announced it has entered into an agreement to acquire Premier Dealer Holding Corp., and its subsidiaries including Premier Dealer Services (PDS), a Dublin, Ohio-based provider of automotive Finance and Insurance (F&I) products and services.

The acquisition, upon completion, will build on a long-standing relationship between Arch Insurance and PDS, combining Arch’s deep specialty insurance expertise with PDS’s administration capabilities, technology infrastructure and relationships.

“PDS has built a strong business with an experienced team, differentiated technology and extensive dealer relationships,” said Matt Shulman, CEO of Arch Insurance North America. “We know the company well. Bringing PDS and Arch together will strengthen our capabilities in the automotive F&I market and create new opportunities to serve our customers and partners.”

“Arch has been a trusted partner to Premier for many years, and we know and respect their team,” said John Topits, CEO of PDS. “Joining Arch gives us the financial strength and resources to keep investing in our people, products and technology, while our dealers and agents continue working with the same Premier team they know today.”

Following completion of the transaction, PDS is expected to operate as a standalone business within Arch Insurance’s Consumer Division.

This transaction is expected to close by the end of 2026 and is subject to regulatory approvals and satisfaction of other customary closing conditions.

TD Securities is acting as the exclusive financial advisor to Arch, and Eversheds Sutherland LLP is serving as Arch’s legal advisor.

About Arch Insurance North America

Arch Insurance North America, part of Arch Capital Group Ltd., includes Arch’s insurance operations in the United States and Canada. Business in the U.S. is written by Arch Insurance Company, Arch Specialty Insurance Company, Arch Property & Casualty Insurance Company and Arch Indemnity Insurance Company. Business in Canada is written by Arch Insurance Canada Ltd.

About Arch Capital Group Ltd.

Arch Capital Group Ltd. (Nasdaq: ACGL) is a publicly listed Bermuda exempted company with approximately $27.3 billion in capital at September 30, 2026. Arch, which is part of the S&P 500 Index, provides insurance, reinsurance and mortgage insurance on a worldwide basis through its wholly owned subsidiaries.

About Premier Dealer Services

Founded in 1998 and headquartered in Dublin, Ohio, Premier Dealer Services (PDS) is a leading provider of loyalty and automotive protection products and customized services for dealerships. Through its technology platform, dealer training and long-standing dealer relationships, PDS builds programs that increase dealer profitability across every area of the dealership while building long-term sales and service retention for our dealer customers. Learn more at pdsadm.com.

BERWICK, Pa.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--First Keystone Corporation (OTCID: FKYS), parent company of First Keystone Community Bank, reported an increase in total interest income of $3,195,000 or 5.6%, as compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was predominantly due to interest earned on increased balances of interest-bearing deposits held at the Federal Reserve Bank compared to the same period in 2025. Total interest expense increased by $957,000 or 3.3% overall, mainly due to an increase of $675,000 in interest expense related to interest paid on the Bank’s outstanding subordinated debt due to the contracted change from fixed to floating rate which transpired in 2026. The rate paid on the subordinated debt increased from 4.375% fixed to a floating rate which was equivalent to 7.745% as of the September 30, 2026 interest payment. The net effect of derivative agreements decreased net interest income by $809,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and increased net interest income by $586,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. These derivative agreements are part of the Corporation’s interest rate risk management strategy and are intended to mitigate exposure to changes in market interest rates. The provision for credit losses for the nine month period decreased by $1,894,000 to a recovery of credit losses of $1,125,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to expense of $769,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The recovery of credit losses for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was mainly the result of a decrease of $640,000 in the provision for credit losses related to the Bank’s owner-occupied, non-farm, non-residential loans. Of the $640,000, a decrease of $440,000 was due to a reduction in specific allocation on an individually evaluated loan and a decrease of $200,000 was attributable to a decrease in the outstanding principal balance of owner-occupied, non-farm, non-residential loans of $1,954,000, along with a decrease in the related quantitative loss rate. The Bank also experienced decreases in outstanding principal balance and quantitative loss rates related to pooled/collectively evaluated loans in two of the Bank’s larger loan categories: multifamily loans and non-owner occupied, non-farm, non-residential loans. The outstanding principal balance of pooled/collectively evaluated loans related to these two categories decreased by $7,659,000 and $3,710,000 during the nine months ended September 30, 2026. The provision for credit losses related to these categories decreased by $329,000 and $189,000, respectively as of the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Non-interest income increased by $594,000 or 10.9% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the same period in 2025. Net securities gains improved by $537,000 to a gain of $665,000 compared to a gain of $128,000 as a result of changes in the mark-to-market adjustment on held equity securities. Other non-interest income decreased $201,000 mainly due to $255,000 in gains from life insurance proceeds realized from a death benefit received during the first nine months of 2025, offset by a recovery of $49,000 on a prior defalcation loss, an increase of $45,000 in ATM and debit card fees, and an increase of $30,000 in income related to bank owned life insurance recorded during the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Non-interest expense increased by $1,309,000 or 5.3% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the same period in 2025. The increase was mainly due to a $605,000 increase in salaries and employee benefits, a $444,000 increase in professional services expense, a $366,000 increase in furniture, equipment and computers expense, an increase of $90,000 in ATM and debit card expenses, and an increase of $88,000 in data processing fees, offset by a decrease of $307,000 in other non-interest expense related to a fraud write off associated with a customer account realized in the first quarter of 2025.

Net income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $9,475,000. Net income per share was $1.50 while dividends totaled $0.84 per share for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. Net income increased by $2,700,000 or 39.9% as compared to the same period in 2025. The increase was primarily due to increased interest income and a decrease in the provision for credit losses.

Total assets increased to $1,726,469,000 at September 30, 2026, an increase of $144,092,000 or 9.1% as compared to September 30, 2025. Cash and cash equivalents increased by $184,869,000 or 125.5% as compared to September 30, 2025 mainly due to increased deposit balances during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, offset with a decrease in the balance of securities and restricted stocks, as discussed below, and a decrease in the balance of loans which resulted from regular principal payments and paydowns outpacing new loan originations for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. Securities and restricted stocks decreased $34,082,000 or 8.1% as compared to September 30, 2025 mainly due to a decrease in securities balances of $34,877,000 which resulted from $64,025,000 in maturities, calls, and paydowns and a decline of $9,718,000 in the fair value adjustment on securities between September 30, 2025 and September 30, 2026, offset by investment purchases of $42,598,000 in 2026. Deposits increased by $123,299,000 or 10.3% at September 30, 2026 as compared to September 30, 2025 due to increases in retail CDs offset with decreases in other retail deposits and brokered CDs. Stockholders’ equity increased $1,012,000 or 0.9% mainly due to increases in retained earnings and surplus of $1,813,000 and $1,233,000, respectively, offset by an increase of $2,187,000 in accumulated other comprehensive loss.

The review period for subsequent events extends up to and including the filing date of a public company’s consolidated financial statements when filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”). Accordingly, the financial information in this announcement is subject to change.

ELMER, N.J.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--ELMER BANCORP, INC. (“Elmer Bancorp” or the “Company”) (OTCID: ELMA), the parent company of The First National Bank of Elmer (the “Bank”), announces its operating results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, Elmer Bancorp reported net income of $786,000, or $0.68 per average diluted common share, compared to $768,000, or $0.67 per average diluted common share for the three months ended September 30, 2025. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, net income totaled $2.195 million or $1.91 per average diluted common share compared to $2.584 million, or $2.26 per average diluted common share for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

Net interest income for the three months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $4.245 million, an increase of $134,000 from $4.111 million in the third quarter of 2025. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, net interest income totaled $12.530 million compared to $11.893 million for the nine-month period of 2025. This increase in net interest income is the result of higher interest and fees on loans and lower interest paid on deposits partially offset by lower income on our overnight investments. The loan loss provision was increased by $70,000 and $160,000 for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to an increase of $40,000 and $124,000 for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025. This adjustment was the result of the required loan loss calculation under the Current Expected Credit Loss (“CECL”) model.

Non-interest income for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $36,000 higher than the same three-month period a year ago and $461,000 lower than the nine-month period last year. Increases in Visa credit card commissions and higher service fee income accounted for the increase in the three-month period. The decrease in the nine-month period was the result of the one-time “BOLI” payout of $530,000 received in the first quarter of 2025 partially offset by higher service fee income.

Non-interest expenses were higher for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 versus the prior year periods by $120,000 and $491,000, respectively. Increases in employment costs, occupancy and equipment costs and data processing costs were partially offset by lower professional fees.

Elmer Bancorp’s total assets at September 30, 2026 totaled $398.1 million, a decrease of $12.1 million from the September 30, 2025 level of $410.2 million. Loans totaled $339.7 million at September 30, 2026, an increase of $16.5 million from the September 30, 2025 total of $323.2 million. This increase in loans was more than offset by a decrease in overnight investments of $25.4 million. At September 30, 2026, the allowance for loan losses was 1.27% of total loans.

Deposits totaled $354.6 million at September 30, 2026, compared to the September 30, 2025 total of $369.2 million, reflecting a decrease of $10.5 million in interest bearing deposits and a decrease of $4.1 million in non-interest-bearing deposits. The September 30, 2025 balance included $5.0 million in short term borrowings which have since been re-paid and outlier deposit fluctuations of several large clients. In addition, the collection and growth of deposits continues to be highly competitive and rate sensitive. Stockholders’ equity totaled $40.8 million at September 30, 2026. The book value per share at September 30, 2026 was $35.23 compared to $33.36 per share at September 30, 2025. The Bank met all regulatory capital requirements to be classified as a well-capitalized institution as of September 30, 2026.

Brian W. Jones, President and Chief Executive Officer stated, “Our third quarter results remain strong highlighted by our solid loan growth of $16.5 million year-over-year. Net income continues to be consistent and at sustained levels. We remain confident in our ability to drive value for our shareholders as we continue to build shareholder equity. As always, we would like to thank our customers, shareholders and employees for their steadfast support.”

The First National Bank of Elmer, a nationally chartered bank headquartered in Elmer, New Jersey, has a long history of serving the community since its beginnings in 1903. We are a community bank focused on providing deposit and loan products to retail customers and to small and mid-sized businesses from our six full-service branch offices located in Cumberland, Gloucester and Salem Counties, New Jersey, including our main office located at 10 South Main Street in Elmer, New Jersey. In addition to our branch offices, the bank also operates a loan production office (“LPO”) located in Marlton, NJ to service our clients in Burlington County. Deposits at The First National Bank of Elmer are insured up to the legal maximum amount by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (“FDIC”).

For more information about Elmer Bank and its products and services, please visit our website at www.ElmerBank.com or call toll free 1-856-358-7000.

NEW YORK, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- SVRN, Inc. (NASDAQ: SVRN) ("SVRN" or the "Company"), formerly OceanPal Inc., today announced that on October 30th, 2026 it received a letter from the Listing Qualifications Department of The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC ("Nasdaq") stating that the Company did not meet the terms of the exception previously granted by Nasdaq staff because it had not filed its Annual Report on Form 20-F for the year ended December 31, 2025 (the "2025 Annual Report") by October 27, 2026, and that, as a result, its securities are subject to delisting under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5250(c)(1).

Under Nasdaq rules, a hearing request in a filing delinquency matter stays the suspension of the Company's securities for 15 days from the date of the request, unless the Panel grants a further stay. The Company plans to request a hearing on or before November 6, 2026, and will ask the Panel to extend that stay pending the conclusion of the Hearings process. There can be no assurance that the Panel will grant an extended stay or that the Company will ultimately maintain its Nasdaq listing.

The Company's shares are expected to continue to trade on The Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol "SVRN", at least through the 15-day stay period and, if the Panel grants the extended stay, through the Panel's decision process.

Consultation with the SEC's Office of the Chief Accountant ("OCA")

Under the oversight of its Audit Committee, the Company submitted on October 29, 2026 a pre-filing consultation on the classification of certain of its equity-linked instruments, including its Preferred Stock and certain of its outstanding warrants, which are relevant to completion of the 2025 Annual Report.

The Company elected to pursue a pre-filing consultation with the SEC staff to obtain its views on the Company's proposed accounting treatment for 2025, which, other than the reclassification of the Series C and Series D Preferred Stock to temporary equity, is consistent with its presentation in the Company's previously issued financial statements. SVRN is working with its technical advisors to complete the OCA process, and intends to file the 2025 Annual Report as promptly as practicable after the consultation concludes and within any period the Panel grants. The Company expects to reflect that reclassification as a revision of prior-period amounts in the 2025 Annual Report. However, if the Company receives an unfavorable outcome from this consultation process, it is possible that the Company will need to further revise or restate its previously issued financial statements for prior reporting periods. The timing of the OCA's response is not within the Company's control.

Interim report

The Company also expects that it will not meet the December 31, 2026 deadline under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5250(c)(2) for furnishing its interim financial information for the six months ended June 30, 2026, because completion of that report depends on resolution of the accounting treatment under consultation with the OCA.

Background and operations

As previously disclosed, on May 19, 2026, the Company received notice from Nasdaq that it was not in compliance with Listing Rule 5250(c)(1) because it had not filed the 2025 Annual Report. On August 24, 2026, Nasdaq staff granted the Company an exception through October 27, 2026.

The filing delay does not affect the Company's operations, which continue across its validator and staking operations and its FastNEAR network infrastructure business.

The Company will continue to keep all stakeholders fully updated with material developments with the appropriate disclosures.

SVRN, Inc. (NASDAQ: SVRN) exists to keep individuals in control of their assets, their data, and the AI agents that act on their behalf. At the center of its work is NEAR Protocol, the open infrastructure for the agentic economy. SVRN's strategy comprises actively managing a digital asset treasury anchored by NEAR, driving commercial adoption of NEAR's products, and backing, building, and acquiring ventures that serve its mission. MOOSIC, Pa.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Peoples Financial Services Corp. (“Peoples” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: PFIS), the bank holding company for Peoples Security Bank and Trust Company (the “Bank”), today reported unaudited financial results at and for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Peoples reported net income of $19.1 million, or $1.90 per diluted share for the three months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $3.9 million compared to net income of $15.2 million, or $1.51 per diluted share for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Net income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $48.7 million, or $4.85 per diluted share, an increase of $1.5 million, compared to $47.2 million, or $4.69 per diluted share for the same nine months of 2025. Return on average assets (“ROAA”) and return on average equity (“ROAE”) on an annualized basis for the three months ended September 30, 2026, were 1.41% and 14.07%, respectively, compared to 1.19% and 12.02%, respectively, for the three months ended September 30, 2025. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, annualized ROAA and ROAE were 1.23% and 12.16%, respectively, compared to 1.25% and 12.86%, respectively, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in net income for both the three- and nine-month periods was primarily attributable to higher net interest income and non-interest income, partially offset by increases in non-interest expense. For the three-month period ending September 30, 2026, there was a benefit of credit losses whereas the nine-month period recognized a provision of credit losses that partially offset the increase in net income for the year-to-date period.

“We are pleased with our strong third-quarter performance, highlighted by meaningful growth in net income and improved returns on both assets and equity. Higher net interest income and non-interest income reflect the strength of our core business, the dedication of our team, and our disciplined execution” commented Gerard A. Champi, President & CEO. “These results underscore the resilience and strength of our franchise and our continued focus on creating long-term value for our shareholders. As we move forward, we remain committed on delivering consistent financial performance while continuing to invest in our customers, employees, and the communities we serve.” concluded Mr. Champi.

In addition to evaluating its results of operations in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”), Peoples routinely supplements its evaluation with an analysis of certain non-GAAP financial measures, such as tangible stockholders’ equity, core net income, and tax-equivalent net interest income and related ratios, among others. The reported results included in this release contain items, which Peoples considers non-core, namely net gains and losses on the sale of available for sale investment securities and acquisition-related expenses. Peoples believes the reported non-GAAP financial measures provide information useful to investors in understanding its operating performance and trends. Where non-GAAP disclosures are used in this press release, a reconciliation to the comparable GAAP measure is provided in the accompanying tables. The non-GAAP financial measures Peoples uses may differ from the non-GAAP financial measures of other financial institutions and should not be viewed as a substitute for GAAP.

NOTABLES

  • On a linked quarter basis, total loans increased $60.7 million, or 5.6% annualized, to $4.4 billion as of September 30, 2026, from $4.3 billion as of June 30, 2026, and increased $347.1 million, or 8.6% annualized, from $4.0 billion as of September 30, 2025.
  • Nonperforming assets were $10.3 million as of September 30, 2026, an improvement of $4.4 million from $14.7 million as of June 30, 2026, and $6.5 million from $16.8 million at September 30, 2025. Nonperforming assets represented 0.24% of loans, net and foreclosed assets as of September 30, 2026, versus 0.34% and 0.42% of loans, net and foreclosed assets as of June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025, respectively.
  • On a linked quarter basis, total deposits increased $163.3 million, or 14.4% annualized, to $4.7 billion as of September 30, 2026, from $4.5 billion as of June 30, 2026, and increased $382.4 million, or 8.9%, from $4.3 billion as of September 30, 2025.
  • Book value per common share at September 30, 2026, increased $1.92 to $52.87 from $50.95 at September 30, 2025. Tangible book value per common share, a non-GAAP measure1, increased $2.52 to $42.95 at September 30, 2026, compared to $40.43 at September 30, 2025.

INCOME STATEMENT REVIEW

  • Net income increased $3.9 million, or 25.5%, to $19.1 million from $15.2 million in the year ago quarter and $4.3 million, or 29.2%, from $14.8 million for the three months ending June 30, 2026. Net income increased to $48.7 million, or 3.1%, from $47.2 million for the nine months ending September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively.
  • Net interest margin (“NIM”), calculated on a fully taxable equivalent (“FTE”) basis, a non-GAAP measure1, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, improved 26 basis points to 3.80% as compared to 3.54% for the three months ended September 30, 2025, but contracted 2 basis points from 3.82% for the three months ended June 30, 2026. For the nine months ended September 30, the FTE NIM, a non-GAAP measure1, improved 19 basis points to 3.77% in 2026 from 3.58% in 2025.
  • The FTE yield on interest-earning assets, a non-GAAP measure1, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, increased 15 basis points to 5.71% from 5.56% from the three months ended September 30, 2025, and increased 7 basis points from 5.64% for the three months ended June 30, 2026. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the FTE yield on interest-earning assets, a non-GAAP measure1, was 5.62%, an increase of 4 basis points from 5.58% for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.
  • The cost of funds, which represents the average rate paid on total interest-bearing liabilities, decreased 15 basis points to 2.49% from 2.64% for the three months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025 respectively. The cost of funds increased 9 basis points from 2.40% from the three months ended June 30, 2026. For the nine-month periods ended September 30, the cost of funds was 2.43% in 2026, a reduction of 18 basis points compared to 2.61% for 2025.
  • The cost of interest-bearing deposits decreased 13 basis points to 2.26% for the three months ended September 30, 2026, from 2.39% as of the three months ended September 30, 2025, but increased 12 basis points from 2.14% for the three months ended June 30, 2026. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the cost of interest-bearing deposits decreased 23 basis points to 2.19% from 2.42% for the same nine months of 2025.
  • The cost of total deposits, which includes the impact of noninterest-bearing deposits, was 1.79% for the third quarter of 2026, a decrease of 9 basis points from 1.88% for the third quarter of 2025. However, the cost of total deposits increased 11 basis points compared to 1.68% for the second quarter of 2026. The cost of deposits for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was 1.72%, a decrease of 20 basis points from 1.92% for the comparable period of 2025.

Third Quarter 2026 Results – Comparison to Second Quarter 2026 and Third Quarter 2025

Net interest income increased $6.1 million to $47.3 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $41.2 million for the prior year third quarter. FTE net interest income, a non-GAAP measure1, increased $6.4 million to $48.3 million as of September 30, 2026, from $41.9 million at September 30, 2025. Specifically, the increase in FTE net interest income, a non-GAAP measure1, resulted largely from a $6.5 million increase in FTE interest income, while interest expense increased modestly by $0.2 million. The increase in interest income reflected improved earning asset yields and an increase in loan volume, while lower deposit and borrowing costs almost entirely offset the impact of growth in interest-bearing liabilities on interest expense. Linked quarter net interest income increased $1.7 million from $45.6 million at June 30, 2026. FTE net interest income for the linked quarters increased $1.8 million from $46.5 million in June 2026, which was due to a $3.8 million increase in FTE interest income, partially offset by a $2.0 million increase in interest expense. The linked quarters saw increases in funding costs as the Company utilized CD specials, brokered deposits and FHLB advances to fund loan growth.

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company recorded a benefit for credit losses of $1.1 million, compared to a benefit of $0.8 million for the same period in 2025, and a provision of $3.1 million for the second quarter of 2026. The reduction in credit provisioning reflected improved asset quality metrics, seasoning of the equipment loan segment and lower specific reserves resulting from the successful resolution of nonperforming loans.

Noninterest income was $5.7 million and $5.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively. The Company recorded a loss on the sales of administrative offices of $0.6 million in the third quarter of 2025. There were no such losses recorded during the third quarter of 2026. Non-interest income decreased $0.8 million from $6.5 million for the linked quarter ending June 30, 2026, primarily due to decreases in merchant services and service charges and the absence of the $0.3 million gain on the sale of a branch property that was part of a sale/leaseback transaction in the second quarter of 2026.

The current quarter’s non-interest expense increased $3.0 million to $31.7 million from the prior year’s same quarter non-interest expense of $28.7 million. Salaries and employee benefits increased $1.5 million associated with merit increases, staff additions, and higher benefit costs. Other expenses increased $1.1 million primarily due to increases in corporate business development and professional fees. Noninterest expense increased by $1.1 million from $30.6 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. Salaries increased $0.5 million, which primarily reflected staff additions and higher stock-based compensation expenses. Occupancy and equipment expenses increased $0.4 million resulting from higher data processing expenses. Income tax expense was $3.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $3.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, and $3.6 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026. The effective tax rate was 14.6% for the three months ended September 30, 2026, 19.1% for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, and 19.6% for the three months ended June 30, 2026. The decrease in the effective tax rate for the current quarter was largely due to the purchase of 2025 federal tax credits during the three months ended September 30, 2026, which reduced income tax expense by $1.2 million.

Nine-Month Results – Comparison to Prior Year First Nine Months

Net interest income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, increased $12.9 million to $135.8 million from $122.9 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. On an FTE basis, net interest income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, increased $13.4 million to $138.5 million from $125.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in FTE net interest income was due to an $11.6 million increase in tax-equivalent interest income, a non-GAAP measure1, coupled with a $1.8 million decrease in interest expense. The Company’s net interest spread widened 22 basis points to 3.19% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from 2.97% for the same nine-month period of 2025. Additionally, comparing the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, the Company’s FTE net interest margin improved by 19 basis points to 3.77% from 3.58%, respectively.

The increase in fully tax-equivalent interest income was driven primarily by higher earning asset balances, particularly taxable loans, and by higher balances and yields on tax-exempt investment securities. Lower overall FTE yields, mainly on taxable investments, partially offset these benefits.

Total average earning assets increased $241.4 million to $4.9 billion for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, from $4.7 billion for the same nine months of 2025. Average taxable loans increased $245.4 million to $4.0 billion from $3.7 billion comparing the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively. The yield on taxable loans decreased 10 basis points to 6.03% from 6.13% between the two periods, which primarily reflected a 75 basis point reduction in the prime rate during the second half of 2025 offset slightly by the increase of 25 basis points in September 2026. Accretion associated with purchase accounting fair value discounts on purchased loans was $9.5 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $12.2 million for the same period of 2025. Average tax-exempt investments totaled $157.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $66.7 million from $90.9 million for the same nine-month period ended September 30, 2025, while taxable investments averaged $430.9 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $549.8 million at September 30, 2025. Average interest earning deposits increased by $58.1 million to $100.9 million at September 30, 2026, from $42.8 million at September 30, 2025. The FTE yield on investments increased 76 basis points to 3.87% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, from 3.11% for the same nine months of 2025.

Interest expense decreased $1.8 million to $68.2 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared with $70.0 million for the same period in 2025, primarily due to lower average deposit rates overall, coupled with a reduction in average small dollar time deposits, which offset net balance increases in the non-maturing deposit portfolio. These benefits were partially offset by higher average balances on borrowings and subordinated debt exceeding reductions in borrowing rates. The average rate paid on interest-bearing deposits decreased 23 basis points to 2.19% from 2.42%, reflecting lower market rates in 2026 in addition to lower costs related to interest bearing demand accounts when compared to 2025.

Average small dollar time deposits, which include brokered deposits, decreased $68.5 million to $321.3 million, for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, from $389.8 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The average rate paid for small dollar time deposits decreased 53 basis points to 3.29% from 3.82% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively, partially the result of a reduction of $50.9 million in average brokered deposits, which the Company let roll off at maturity. These higher-costing deposits were replaced with lower cost non-maturing deposits and borrowings. Average subordinated debt increased $25.9 million to $83.3 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, from $57.4 million for the same period in 2025, while the average rate paid on subordinated debt increased 93 basis points to 8.42% from 7.49% for the periods ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively, due to a net new issuance of subordinated debt in the second quarter of 2025 in the amount of $52 million.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the provision for credit losses was $3.3 million, an increase of $4.2 million from a $0.9 million benefit recorded for the same nine months of 2025. The increase in loan provisioning in the first nine months of 2026 was primarily impacted by significant loan growth, while the benefit in the first nine months of the prior year reflected reductions in non-accrual assets and declines in model loss rates.

Noninterest income was $19.1 million and $18.0 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively. The $1.1 million increase in noninterest income was primarily due to increases in interest rate swap income of $0.6 million, along with combined net gains of $0.5 million on the sale of investment securities available for sale, a $0.3 million gain on the sale and market value appreciation of equity securities and a $0.4 million increase in mortgage banking income, partially offset by a decrease in service charge, fee, and commission income of $0.7 million. Noninterest expense increased $7.9 million to $92.2 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, from $84.3 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. This increase is primarily due to increases in salaries and employee benefits expenses, occupancy and equipment expenses, and other expenses. Salaries and employee benefits expense was $45.2 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $41.4 million for the same nine months in 2025. The $3.8 million increase resulted primarily from annual merit increases, staff additions and higher health insurance costs. Net occupancy and equipment expenses were $22.7 million for the first nine months of 2026, an increase of $2.6 million from $20.1 million for the same nine-month period in 2025. The increase was largely caused by higher rent expenses associated with the new corporate headquarters and increases in data processing expenses related to the implementation of an on-line account opening platform. Other expenses increased $2.6 million to $17.7 million from $15.1 million for the nine months ending September 30, 2025. BALANCE SHEET REVIEW

Total loans were $4.4 billion at September 30, 2026, an increase of $60.7 million compared to $4.3 billion at June 30, 2026, and an increase of $347.1 million compared to $4.0 billion at September 30, 2025. Comparing September 30, 2026, and 2025, the Company saw strong demand in all markets for commercial and residential real estate loans, commercial and industrial loans, and municipal loans, with decreases seen in the Company’s equipment financing and indirect auto loan portfolio. Comparing September 30, 2026, to June 30, 2026, increases were observed in the commercial and industrial portfolio and in the commercial and residential real estate portfolio. Consumer loans and the equipment financing portfolios were relatively flat, while the indirect auto portfolio decreased.

Total investments were $510.2 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $529.6 million at June 30, 2026, and $610.3 million at September 30, 2025. At September 30, 2026, available for sale securities totaled $440.8 million, a decrease of $17.3 million from $458.1 million at June 30, 2026, and a decrease of $93.7 million from $534.5 million at September 30, 2025. Held to maturity securities totaled $66.7 million at September 30, 2026, a decrease of $2.1 million from $68.8 million at June 30, 2026, and a decrease of $6.6 million from $73.3 million at September 30, 2025. Due to strong loan demand, cash flows from repayments of investment securities and a portion of the proceeds from sales of investments during the first three months of 2026 were redirected and used to fund loan growth.

Total deposits were $4.7 billion at September 30, 2026, an increase of $163.3 million from $4.5 billion at June 30, 2026, and an increase of $382.4 million from $4.3 billion at September 30, 2025. Noninterest-bearing deposits increased $24.5 million to $971.0 million at September 30, 2026, from $946.5 million at June 30, 2026, and increased $59.1 million from $912.0 million at September 30, 2025. Interest-bearing deposits increased $138.7 million to $3.7 billion from $3.6 billion at June 30, 2026, and increased $323.4 million from $3.4 billion at September 30, 2025, primarily reflecting a strategic deposit growth effort which offset a decrease in brokered deposits. Brokered deposits represented 5.4% of total deposits at September 30, 2026, and 7.7% of total deposits at June 30, 2026, compared with 3.9% at September 30, 2025. Approximately 34.8% of deposits were uninsured at September 30, 2026, compared with 31.0% uninsured at June 30, 2026, and 32.3% at September 30, 2025.

The Company maintained a strong capital position at September 30, 2026. Stockholders’ equity equaled $529.3 million or $52.87 per share at September 30, 2026, compared to $536.2 million or $53.56 per share at June 30, 2026, and $509.3 million, or $50.95 per share at September 30, 2025. Stockholders’ equity was impacted by net income, offset by dividends to shareholders and an increase in accumulated other comprehensive loss primarily due to market rate adjustments related to available for sale investments.

Tangible book value, a non-GAAP measure1 was $42.95 per share at September 30, 2026, $43.51 per share at June 30, 2026, and $40.43 at September 30, 2025. The Company declared quarterly dividends of $0.625 for each quarter of 2026 and $0.6175 for the quarter ending September 30, 2025. Dividends for the year totaled $1.875 per share for 2026 and $1.853 per share for 2025.

ASSET QUALITY REVIEW

The Company experienced strong improvement in asset quality during the three- and nine-month periods of 2026. Nonperforming assets, which include nonperforming loans, loans past due 90 days or more and still accruing, and foreclosed assets, were $10.3 million or 0.24% of loans, net and foreclosed assets, at September 30, 2026, a $4.4 million decrease compared to $14.7 million, or 0.34% of loans, net and foreclosed assets at June 30, 2026. The linked-quarter decrease was primarily due to favorable resolutions of several nonaccrual assets during the third quarter of 2026. In comparison to the prior year period, nonperforming assets decreased $6.5 million from $16.8 million, or 0.42% of loans, net and foreclosed assets at September 30, 2025, primarily reflecting a $4.3 million reduction in nonaccrual loans and the final resolution of a foreclosed property. Nonperforming assets represented 0.19% of total assets at September 30, 2026, compared to 0.27% at June 30, 2026, and 0.33% at September 30, 2025.

Key Terms

roaafinancial
Return on Average Assets (ROAA) measures how efficiently a company turns its assets into profit by dividing net profit over a period by the average total assets it held during that period. It matters to investors because it shows whether a business is getting a good return from what it owns—like judging a car’s fuel efficiency by miles per gallon—helping compare profitability across companies of different sizes.
roaefinancial
ROAE stands for Return on Average Equity, a profitability ratio that shows how much net income a company generates for its owners relative to the average amount of shareholder equity invested over a period. It’s like measuring the interest rate a business pays its owners on the capital they’ve left in the company, with the ‘average’ smoothing out swings in equity during the year. Investors use ROAE to compare how efficiently different companies turn owner capital into profits and to assess management’s ability to deliver returns over time.
gaapfinancial
GAAP, or Generally Accepted Accounting Principles, are a set of standardized rules and guidelines that companies follow when preparing their financial statements. They ensure consistency, transparency, and comparability across different companies, making it easier for investors to understand and compare financial information accurately. This helps investors make informed decisions based on trustworthy and uniform financial reports.

non-gaapfinancial
Non-GAAP refers to financial measures that companies use to show their earnings or performance without including certain expenses or income that are often added back to give a different picture. It matters because it can make a company's results look better or more favorable, but it may also hide important costs, so investors need to look at both GAAP (official rules) and non-GAAP numbers to get a full understanding.

net interest marginfinancial
Net interest margin measures how much a bank earns from lending and investing compared with what it pays for funding, expressed as a percentage of its interest-earning assets. Think of it like a grocery store’s markup: it shows the gap between buying cost and selling price per dollar of goods — here, the cost is interest paid and the sale is interest received. Investors watch it because a higher margin usually means a bank is more profitable and better at managing interest rate and credit conditions.
fully taxable equivalentfinancial
A fully taxable equivalent converts a tax-free yield into the pretax yield you would need from a taxable investment to get the same after-tax return, using an investor’s marginal tax rate. Think of it like inflating a discounted price to the full sticker price so you can compare items side‑by‑side; investors use it to fairly compare tax-exempt securities with taxable alternatives and choose the better after-tax income.
